chapter: Opening and childhood on the West Bank
title: Maternal grandparents, Lewis Taylor and the drowned grandmother
summary: His mother's maiden name was Taylor; he tells of his rough carpenter grandfather and how his grandmother drowned in a well.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What was your mother's maiden name?

Taylor. My mother's father was Lewis Taylor, who was a huntsman and a carpenter. And he was a pretty rough character. Lewis, they used to call him tits because he was a good man with his hands. You see tits, you hit your tit for tat and used to knock a lot of people out. That's what youngsters would fight with their hands, you know. My grandmother, I don't know too much about her because, you see, she died something. She went on to a grocery or something. And what happened was that on her way back home from what I understand, she fell into a well behind a church over in Gretton. She was drowned. I don't know whether it was raining that day or what happened. I really don't know what really happened to my grandmother. But that's the way it was told to me. And I was a very small child at that particular time. I think I was about maybe one or two years of age when all of this happened. But I had beautiful pictures of my grandmother. I still have them, but they're somewhere in my files. But God bless her soul.
